    Important National Parks, Wildlife Sanctuaries
    and Biosphere Reserves in India

       📌National Parks – It is the protected areas, which are established by the
              government, to conserve wildlife and also develop them. Human activities are
              not allowed. NP cannot be downgraded to Wildlife Sanctuary. National Parks
             and Wildlife Sanctuaries are created under the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972.


       📌Wildlife Sanctuaries – It is a natural habitat, owned by the government or
                 private agency, that safeguards particular species of birds and animals.
                Limited human activities are allowed. WS can be upgraded to be classified as
              a National Park.


       📌Biosphere Reserves – It is an international designation by UNESCO for an area
              which is set aside for the conservation of the resources of the biosphere and
                  for the improvement of the relationship between man and environment.


        📌Eco-Sensitive Zones – Under the section 3 of the Environment (Protection)
               Act, 1986, the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change notifies the
               land falling within 10 km of the boundaries of national parks and sanctuaries as
                eco-fragile zones.
